# Two windows are two toplevels on gtk4, both on screen once `run` is called,
# and none when `@run` never calls it -- the Wayland protocol log counts them.
# fyne reaches the display through Xwayland, so its runs assert only that the
# program started, ran its timer and ended as written.
#
# testdata/window_several.txtar is the code.

[!headless] skip 'needs the headless compositor go tool verify provides'

[gtk4] sngl build --lang go --platform gtk4 -o gtk4 app.sngl
[gtk4] exec sh -c 'WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 ./gtk4/app --show 2>&1 | grep -c "xdg_toplevel.*set_title" || true'
[gtk4] stdout '^2$'
[gtk4] exec sh -c 'WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 ./gtk4/app 2>&1 | grep -c "xdg_toplevel.*set_title" || true'
[gtk4] stdout '^0$'

sngl build --lang go --platform fyne -o fyne app.sngl
exec ./fyne/app --show
exec ./fyne/app

-- app.sngl --
import go "sngl:language/go"
import time "sngl:time"
import ui "sngl:ui"

#[go.native("os", "os.Exit")]
func exit(code int)

output {
    go {
        gtk4(@run(args, run) {
            if args.contains("--show") {
                run()
            }
        })
        fyne(@run(args, run) {
            if args.contains("--show") {
                run()
            }
        })
    }
}

var ticks = 0

time.timer(interval=200ms, @tick {
    ticks += 1
    if ticks == 2 {
        exit(0)
    }
})

ui.window #main(title="Main") {
    ui.text(value="{ticks}")
}

ui.window #log(title="Log") {
    ui.text(value="log")
}
